title: Reference-tier rung lets one low-effort operator-attested session corroborate
body:
derivePromotion (src/qa/ticket.ts:163-171) treats ANY reference-tier report as corroborating on its own, and operator_attested sessions count. The grok wave (bin/playtest-grok-wave.ts) pins grok-4.6 — tier "reference" in blind-tester/catalogs/grok_cli.json — at reasoning_effort=low with a client tool boundary that is prompt-restricted but not independently audited. Net: one cheap, unaudited-client session's opinion can promote a ticket into intake/queue with no second family, which sits oddly against "reference = expensive calibration instrument" (src/blind/providers.ts:110-128).

Decide one: (a) the reference rung requires runner_enforced isolation; (b) grok-4.6-at-low-effort loses the reference tier in the catalog; or (c) this is accepted and documented where the tiers are defined. Any of the three closes the gap; today the policy and the catalog disagree silently.

From the 2026-08-30 full audit, findings ledger P3.

evidence.summary: 2026-08-30 audit: promotion policy vs reference-tier semantics
